cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubis bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the opposite pubis at the pubic symphysis and contributes to the acetabulum and obturator foramen.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, superior ramus, inferior ramus, pubic crest, pubic tubercle and pecten pubis.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Provides attachment for adductor muscles, gracilis, rectus abdominis and pelvic/perineal structures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ischium bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Contributes to the acetabulum and joins the pubis anteriorly and ilium superiorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Ischial spine, ischial tuberosity, lesser sciatic notch and ramus.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Provides attachment for hamstrings, sacrotuberous ligament and several pelvic/perineal muscles.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ilium bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with sacrum at the sacroiliac joint and contributes to the acetabulum.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Iliac crest, ASIS, AIIS, PSIS, PIIS, iliac fossa and greater sciatic notch.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Provides broad attachment for abdominal, gluteal and iliacus muscles.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Iliac crest

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Superior border of the ilium.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Attachment for abdominal wall muscles, fascia lata and back muscles.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Highest point is near the L4 vertebral level and is used as a surface landmark.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Acetabulum

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Cup-shaped socket formed by ilium, ischium and pubis.

cards.question: Articulation
cards.answer: Articulates with the head of the femur to form the hip joint.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Lunate surface, acetabular fossa and acetabular notch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ischial tuberosity

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Inferior roughened prominence of the ischium.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Hamstrings, adductor magnus and sacrotuberous ligament attach here.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Weight-bearing point when sitting; important landmark for pudendal nerve blocks.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubic symphysis

cards.question: Type
cards.answer: Secondary cartilaginous joint between the bodies of the pubic bones.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides a strong midline union with slight mobility, increasing during pregnancy.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies anterior to the urinary bladder.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacrum

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with L5, both ilia and the coccyx.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Sacral promontory, foramina, ala, sacral canal and sacral hiatus.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms posterior wall of the pelvis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coccyx

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates superiorly with the sacrum.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Attachment for levator ani, coccygeus, gluteus maximus and anococcygeal ligament.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Curves anteriorly from the sacrum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: 5th lumbar vertebra

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates superiorly with L4 and inferiorly with the sacrum.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the lumbosacral junction at L5–S1.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important level for lumbosacral angle and load transmission into the pelvis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacral promontory

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Anterior projecting margin of the body of S1.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Marks the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Used in obstetric assessment of pelvic dimensions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacrotuberous ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from sacrum/coccyx and posterior ilium to the ischial tuberosity.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stabilises the sacroiliac region and converts sciatic notches into foramina with the sacrospinous ligament.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms part of the boundary of the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Obturator membrane

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Closes most of the obturator foramen, attaching to its bony margins.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides muscle attachment and leaves the obturator canal for neurovascular passage.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Obturator nerve and vessels pass through the obturator canal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Iliacus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the hip and assists lateral rotation; with psoas major forms iliopsoas.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Iliac fossa and inner lip of iliac crest.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lesser trochanter via iliopsoas tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Psoas major muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the hip and trunk; assists lateral rotation and stabilises lumbar spine.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Anterior rami of L1–L3.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Bodies, discs and transverse processes of T12–L5.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lesser trochanter via iliopsoas tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Piriformis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates extended thigh, abducts flexed thigh and stabilises hip.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to piriformis (S1–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior surface of sacrum.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior border of greater trochanter.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Obturator internus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates extended thigh, abducts flexed thigh and stabilises hip.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to obturator internus (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Pelvic surface of obturator membrane and surrounding bone.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial surface of greater trochanter.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Bulbospongiosus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Compresses vestibular bulb and greater vestibular gland; narrows vaginal opening and assists clitoral erection.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of pudendal nerve (S2–S4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Perineal body.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Perineal membrane, clitoral tissues and surrounding fascia.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ischiocavernosus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Compresses the crus of clitoris and helps maintain clitoral erection.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of pudendal nerve (S2–S4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischial tuberosity and ischiopubic ramus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Crus of clitoris/perineal membrane.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External anal sphincter

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Voluntarily constricts the anal canal and contributes to faecal continence.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Inferior rectal nerve from pudendal nerve (S2–S4), with S4 contribution.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Perineal body and tissues around anal canal.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Anococcygeal ligament/coccyx region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep transverse perineal muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supports the perineal body and pelvic floor and helps stabilise pelvic viscera.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of pudendal nerve (S2–S4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischiopubic ramus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Perineal body and contralateral fibres.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Levator ani muscle group

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms most of the pelvic diaphragm, supports pelvic viscera and contributes to urinary and faecal continence.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Mainly nerve to levator ani (S3–S4), with contributions from pudendal nerve.

cards.question: Components
cards.answer: Pubococcygeus and iliococcygeus are major components; puborectalis is also usually included anatomically.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubococcygeus muscle
cards.label: 17a

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supports pelvic viscera and contributes to pelvic floor elevation and continence.
cards.label: 17a

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4), with pudendal contribution.
cards.label: 17a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Body of pubis and anterior tendinous arch of obturator fascia.
cards.label: 17a

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Perineal body, walls of pelvic viscera, anococcygeal body and coccyx region.
cards.label: 17a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Iliococcygeus muscle
cards.label: 17b

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supports pelvic viscera and elevates the pelvic floor.
cards.label: 17b

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4).
cards.label: 17b

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Tendinous arch of obturator fascia and ischial spine.
cards.label: 17b

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Anococcygeal body/raphe and coccyx.
cards.label: 17b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coccygeus muscle (not a member of levator ani)
cards.label: 17c

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supports pelvic viscera and draws coccyx anteriorly after defecation.
cards.label: 17c

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Anterior rami of S4–S5.
cards.label: 17c

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischial spine and sacrospinous ligament.
cards.label: 17c

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral margins of lower sacrum and coccyx.
cards.label: 17c

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superficial transverse perineal muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Stabilises the perineal body.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of pudendal nerve (S2–S4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischial tuberosity.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Perineal body.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Greater vestibular gland (Bartholin's gland)
cards.label: 19a

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Secretes mucus that lubricates the vestibule, particularly during sexual arousal.
cards.label: 19a

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Posterolateral to the vaginal opening in the superficial perineal pouch, deep to bulbospongiosus.
cards.label: 19a

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Duct opens into the vestibule near the posterolateral vaginal opening.
cards.label: 19a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Bulb of vestibule
cards.label: 19b

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired elongated masses of erectile tissue flanking the vaginal opening.
cards.label: 19b

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Engorge during sexual arousal and contribute to narrowing of the vaginal opening.
cards.label: 19b

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Covered by bulbospongiosus muscle and lie in the superficial perineal pouch.
cards.label: 19b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep transverse perineal muscle and perineal membrane

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps stabilise the perineal body; the perineal membrane provides a strong fascial support across the urogenital triangle.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Deep transverse perineal muscle lies in the deep perineal pouch adjacent to the perineal membrane.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Perineal membrane attaches laterally to the ischiopubic rami.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Labium majus

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired hair-bearing skin folds containing fat and connective tissue.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Protects the more medial vulval structures.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies lateral to the labium minus and extends from mons pubis toward the perineum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Labium minus

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired thin hairless skin folds lacking substantial fat.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Borders the vestibule and protects urethral and vaginal openings.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies medial to labium majus and forms prepuce/frenulum around the clitoris anteriorly.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Clitoris

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Erectile sensory organ involved in sexual arousal.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Root, body and glans; paired crura form the root.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Somatic sensation mainly via dorsal nerve of clitoris from pudendal nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Prepuce

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Fold of skin formed by anterior union of the labia minora over the glans clitoris.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Covers and protects the glans clitoris.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External opening of urethra

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Opens into the vestibule anterior to the vaginal opening.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: External outlet for urine.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External opening of vagina

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Opens into the vestibule posterior to the external urethral opening.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: External opening of the vaginal canal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vestibule of vagina

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Space between the labia minora.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Contains the external urethral and vaginal openings and openings of greater vestibular glands.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Receives openings of urinary and reproductive tracts.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior fascia of urogenital diaphragm

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Older terminology generally corresponding to the perineal membrane.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Supports structures of the urogenital triangle and provides muscular/fascial attachment.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the inferior boundary of the deep perineal pouch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Bifurcation of abdominal aorta at about L4.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs inferolaterally to divide into external and internal iliac arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvis and lower limb through terminal branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of common iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs along pelvic brim and passes under inguinal ligament to become femoral artery.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Main arterial route to lower limb; also lower anterior abdominal wall.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of common iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends into lesser pelvis and divides into anterior and posterior divisions.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvic viscera/walls, gluteal region and perineum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Obturator artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually anterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs on lateral pelvic wall through obturator canal.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medial thigh, hip region and pelvic structures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior vesical artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually arises from patent proximal umbilical artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes to superior bladder.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Superior urinary bladder and distal ureter.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Uterine artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs medially in base of broad ligament, crosses superior to ureter, then ascends along uterus.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Uterus, cervix, upper vagina and uterine tube via branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior gluteal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Exits greater sciatic foramen superior to piriformis.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Gluteal region and adjacent muscles.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior gluteal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Exits greater sciatic foramen inferior to piriformis.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Gluteal region and proximal posterior thigh.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal pudendal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Exits greater sciatic foramen, hooks around ischial spine, enters lesser sciatic foramen and pudendal canal.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Perineum and external genitalia.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac vein

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Union of external and internal iliac veins.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends to join the opposite common iliac vein.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Right and left common iliac veins form the inferior vena cava.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior vena cava

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Formed by union of right and left common iliac veins, usually at L5.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends on the right side of the vertebral column.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Returns venous blood from lower limbs, pelvis and abdomen to the right atrium.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sciatic nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S3 from the sacral plexus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Leaves pelvis through greater sciatic foramen inferior to piriformis and descends in posterior thigh.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies posterior thigh and, via tibial/common fibular branches, most muscles below the knee.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Indirectly supplies most of leg and foot through terminal branches.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Proximal injury can cause weakness of knee flexion and severe weakness or paralysis of movements below the knee, with sensory loss over much of the leg and foot; the exact pattern depends on the level and which tibial/common fibular fibres are affected.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacral plexus

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S4 anterior rami via lumbosacral trunk and sacral nerves.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: On posterolateral pelvic wall, anterior to piriformis.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Includes sciatic, superior/inferior gluteal, pudendal, posterior femoral cutaneous and other nerves.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Rectouterine pouch (pouch of Douglas)

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Peritoneal recess between posterior uterus/cervix and anterior rectum.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Lowest part of the female peritoneal cavity when upright; fluid may collect here.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Can be accessed through the posterior vaginal fornix.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Peritoneum

cards.question: Definition
cards.answer: Serous membrane lining the abdominopelvic cavity and covering intraperitoneal viscera.

cards.question: Layers
cards.answer: Parietal peritoneum lines the wall; visceral peritoneum covers organs.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms pelvic reflections including vesicouterine and rectouterine pouches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Rectum

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stores faeces before defecation.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Begins at rectosigmoid junction around S3 and continues to anorectal junction.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Posterior to uterus and vagina; rectouterine pouch lies anteriorly in its upper part.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Superior rectal artery with middle/inferior rectal contributions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Uterus

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Site of implantation and fetal development; myometrium contracts in labour.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Fundus, body, isthmus and cervix.

cards.question: Position
cards.answer: Normally anteverted and anteflexed.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Mainly uterine artery with ovarian artery anastomoses.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Bladder anterior and rectum posterior.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Isthmus of uterine tube (Fallopian tube)

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Narrow medial segment between ampulla and uterine part.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Conducts gametes/early embryo toward the uterus.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Runs within the superior free margin of the broad ligament.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ampulla of uterine tube (Fallopian tube)

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Wider, longest portion of the uterine tube lateral to the isthmus.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Usual site of fertilisation.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Common site of tubal ectopic pregnancy.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fimbriae of uterine tube

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Finger-like projections of the infundibulum of the uterine tube.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Help sweep the ovulated oocyte toward the tubal opening.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lie adjacent to the ovary; one fimbria is attached to the ovary.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ovary

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces oocytes and secretes oestrogens/progesterone.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Usually on lateral pelvic wall in ovarian fossa.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Ovarian ligament, suspensory ligament and mesovarium.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Ovarian artery with uterine artery anastomosis.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Para-aortic lymph nodes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ovarian ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Medial ovary to lateral uterus just inferior to uterine tube.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Anchors ovary to uterus.

cards.question: Embryology
cards.answer: Derived from gubernaculum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Round ligament of the uterus

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Uterine horn to labium majus via deep inguinal ring and inguinal canal.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps maintain uterine anteversion.

cards.question: Embryology
cards.answer: Derived from gubernaculum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Broad ligament of the uterus

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Double layer of peritoneum extending from lateral uterus toward pelvic walls.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Mesometrium, mesosalpinx and mesovarium.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Related to uterine tube, ovarian/uterine vessels, ligaments, nerves and connective tissue.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Supports and suspends female reproductive structures within the pelvis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Rectouterine fold

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Peritoneal fold extending posteriorly from cervix/uterus toward sacrum, overlying uterosacral supporting tissues.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms lateral boundaries of the rectouterine pouch.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contributes to uterine/cervical support.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vagina

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Canal for intercourse, menstrual flow and childbirth.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Extends from vestibule to cervix.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Posterior to urethra/bladder and anterior to rectum.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Upper part visceral autonomic; lower part somatic via pudendal nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fornix of the vagina

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Recess around the cervix where it projects into the vagina.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Anterior, posterior and lateral fornices.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Posterior fornix lies close to the rectouterine pouch.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Posterior fornix can provide access to the rectouterine pouch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urinary bladder

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stores urine and expels it during micturition.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Apex, body, fundus/base and neck.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Posterior to pubic symphysis and anterior to uterus/vagina.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parasympathetic S2–S4 promotes voiding; sympathetic T11–L2 supports storage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trigone of the bladder

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Smooth triangular area of bladder mucosa between the two ureteric orifices and internal urethral orifice.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Funnels urine toward bladder neck/urethra.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Unlike most bladder mucosa, firmly adherent to underlying muscle.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urethra

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Conducts urine from bladder to exterior.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Short female urethra passes inferoanteriorly from bladder neck to vestibule.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies anterior to vagina.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Short length contributes to increased risk of ascending urinary infection.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ureter

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transports urine from renal pelvis to bladder by peristalsis.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends retroperitoneally, crosses pelvic brim and runs on lateral pelvic wall before entering bladder.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Passes inferior to uterine artery near cervix — 'water under the bridge'.

cards.question: Constrictions
cards.answer: Pelviureteric junction, pelvic brim/iliac vessel crossing and vesicoureteric junction.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: At risk during hysterectomy because of close relation to uterine artery.
